newsitem.title: IRAQ: Iraqi Kurd militia attacks rival on three fronts.
newsitem.headline: Iraqi Kurd militia attacks rival on three fronts.

text.p: SALAHUDDIN, Iraq, Oct 19 - A Kurdish faction captured the northern Iraqi town of Ranya early on Saturday as part of their advance on Sulaimaniya, the stronghold of the rival Patriotic Union of Kurdistan (PUK).

"We took Ranya this morning and we are close to taking Qala Diza," an official of the Kurdistan Democratic Party (KDP) told Reuters in the KDP headquarters in the town of Salahuddin, 50 miles (80 km) west of Ranya.

The KDP was attacking the PUK on three fronts -- around Ranya and the nearby Qala Diza; at Chuman to the northeast close to the border with Iran; and the towns of Khalakan and Kani Watman close to the key Dukan Dam south of Ranya, he said.
The Dukan Dam supplies power to most of the area round the main regional city of Arbil.
The latest fighting between the KDP and the PUK dates back to August 31, when the KDP sought help from Iraqi forces to capture the one-time jointly-shared city of Arbil from the PUK.
Baghdad's intervention on the side of the KDP provoked U.S. cruise missile attacks on southern Iraq and a widening of the no-fly zone there.
The KDP went on to capture the whole of the three Kurdish provinces in the region but last week the PUK began a counter-assault, retaking its stronghold of Sulaimaniya and advancing back to Arbil.
There has been no sign that Baghdad was involved this time around.

Senior U.S. diplomat Robert Pelletreau was due to hold talks with KDP leader Massoud Barzani next week -- probably in Turkey -- to try and hammer out an end to the latest conflict between the two Kurdish groups.
Barzani on Thursday raised the stakes of the peace bid by threatening to call on help from Iraqi President Saddam Hussein against Jalal Talabani's PUK.

In Friday's fighting, the PUK bombarded the village of Hareer, some 80 km (50 miles) north of Salahuddin, killing five civilians including three children, residents said. Six people were injured, a KDP spokesman said.
The PUK was not immediately available for comment.
Washington has said it now will evacuate hundreds of Kurds who worked for U.S.-affiliated organisations in northern Iraq, nominally under Western protection since the end of the 1991 Gulf War.

"They should cross around lunchtime today. They will eventually go to (the Pacific island of) Guam," a Turkish border official said. He put the total number of evacuees, including family members, at 730.

The U.S. evacuated more than 2,000 Kurds, including family, who had worked for them as drivers, translators, guides, computer operators and reportedly even as spies, after Baghdad intervened in last month's fighting.
The KDP official in Salahuddin said the party's peshmerga guerrillas aimed to surround Sulaimaniya by taking towns around the city before closing in for the final kill.
The capture of Ranya and attack on Chuman was part of a strategy to assault a series of positions near the Iranian border to cut off the PUK from what the KDP says are its Iranian allies.

The Kurds broke from Baghdad at the end of the 1991 Gulf War and set up a power-sharing parliament in Arbil. The area is essentially off-limits to the Bahgdad government because of a U.S.-led air operation to protect the Kurds in the country's north.
